idea.body: Two triangles are congruent when all six matching parts, three sides and three angles, are equal, but you never need to check all six. Three tests are enough. SSS: all three pairs of sides match. SAS: two pairs of sides match, and the angle between them, the included angle, also matches. ASA: two pairs of angles match, and the side between them matches. AAS: two pairs of angles match, and a side not between them matches too. A right triangle has one more test, HL: the hypotenuse and one leg match. A test called SSA, two sides and a non-included angle, does not work. It can describe two different triangles, not just one, so it never proves congruence.

workedExample.prompt: Two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides, and the angle between those two sides in each triangle is also congruent. Which test proves the triangles congruent?
steps: Two pairs of sides are marked congruent in each triangle.
The angle between those two sides, the included angle, is also marked congruent.
Two sides and the included angle between them is exactly the SAS test.
So the triangles are congruent by SAS.

ways.name: Match the three parts to the test
ways.when: Use this when the figure already shows which parts are marked congruent.
steps: Two triangles each show two pairs of congruent sides.

ways.trap: Picking SSA instead, when the marked angle is actually between the two marked sides.

ways.name: Mark the figure, then read the test
ways.when: Use this when the congruent parts are described in words, not already marked on the figure.
steps: A problem says two triangles have all three pairs of sides congruent.
Mark each pair of sides you are told about: one tick, two ticks, three ticks.
All three sides marked, with no angle needed, is exactly the SSS test.
So the triangles are congruent by SSS.

ways.trap: Searching for an angle to mark, even though all three side pairs already prove it.

ways.name: The reflection that carries one triangle onto the other
ways.when: Use this when you can see how to flip one triangle onto the other exactly.
steps: Kite ABCD has a diagonal BD splitting it into triangle ABD and triangle CBD.
Triangle CBD is the mirror image of triangle ABD, reflected across BD.
A reflection keeps every length and angle exactly the same.
Since a reflection carries one triangle onto the other, they are congruent.
ways.example: Kite ABCD has diagonal BD. Triangle CBD is the mirror image of triangle ABD across BD. Are they congruent, and why?
ways.answer: yes, a reflection carries one onto the other
ways.trap: Assuming triangles must look congruent by side markings alone, missing that a rigid motion is proof enough.
